Mr. Moinul Huq, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate- on-- Record ----- for the Petitioners.

full_judgment:
2. The background of these matters, briefly, is that one Kusum kumari Debi filed Title Suit No. 75 of 1969 on 20.3.1969 in the First Court of Munsif, Chandpur against one Julmat Dhali, predecessor of the present petitioners and others for permanent injunction in respect of 4.43 acres of land as described in the plaint, The suit was decreed and an appeal was taken against the said decree, The appellate Court passed an order of remand directing the trial Court to try the suit analogously with Title Suit No. 288 of 1969 which was filed on 24.11.1969 by the aforesaid Julmat Dhali for specific performance of contract for sate of the same suit land against kusun Kumari Debi and her husband Bipin Behari, alleging, inter alia, that an oral contract was entered into between the parties in the month of Kartic 1370 B. S. followed by party payment of the consideration of Tk. 3500 and delivery of possession of the suit land. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of Title Suit no. 288 of 1969 filed a written statement but it appears that they did not contest the suit as during the pendency of the suit they made a transfer of the suit land in 1976 by registered deeds to defendant-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 herein who were added in the said suit as defendant Nos. 4 and 5. These defendants contested the suit by filing a written statement subsequently taking the same defence as that of their vendors. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge, Chandpur who held the trials by his judgment and decree dated 28 November 1985 decreed Title Suit No. 288 of 1969 and dismissed Title Suit No.75 1969. 

 5. Defendant- respondent Nos. 1 and 2 took two appeals, Title Appeal Nos. 155 and 156 of 1985 against the decrees passed in the aforesaid two suits and the learned District Judge, Chandpur by his judgment and decree dated 7 February 1987 set aside those of the trial Court and decreed Title Suit No.75 of 1969 and dismissed the other suit i.e. Title Suit No. 288 of 1969. By the impugned judgment and order the said appellate decrees have been affirmed. 

 6. Mr. Moinul Huq, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that he has not much reason to make a grievance of the dismissal of the suit for specific performance of contract (T. S. No. 288 of 1969) but the suit for permanent injunction (T. S. No. 75 of 1969) ought not to have been decreed because the trial Court found the documents of purchase of the contesting defendants to be void and illegal and the learned Judge of the High Court Division misdirected himself in holding that the trial Court had wrongly considered the title of the contesting defendants which shows that the a learned Judge was oblivious that there was a suit for permanent injunction also at the instance of the vendors of the contesting defendants. 

 7. It appears that the trial Court, inter alia, observed that the Kabalas of the contesting defendants obtained from their vendors, defendants No. 1 and 2, were not registered at the proper Sub-Registry Office and as such the documents were void and illegal. It was found that the predecessor of the petitioners Julmat Dhali got delivery of the suit land from defendants No 1 and 2 following the oral agreement of purchase in Kartick 1370 B. S. The learned District Judge, however, in appeal disbelieved the alleged oral contract for sale of the suit land and made a clear finding that possession was not delivered to Julmat Dhali in pursuance of the alleged contract for sale. As regards the finding of the trial Court in respect of the kabalas of the contesting defendants the learned District Judge observed that since it was not a title suit no finding could be, arrived at with regard to the title of the contesting defendants and the kabalas filed by them were evidence of prima facie title in a suit for permanent injunction. 

 8. Admittedly the vendors of the contesting defendants had title and possession in the suit land and the petitioners' suit for specific performance of contract having failed, there was no difficulty in decreeing the suit for permanent injunction in the circumstances found by the appellate Court even though the contesting defendants had come in the picture in the meantime on the basis of their alleged purchase by registered documents. Whether they acquired valid title or not was not or could not be a prime issue in the suit for permanent injunction in which the question of possession was the main consideration. The learned District Judge, in our opinion, has taken a correct view of the matter and therefore notwithstanding certain observations in the judgment of the High Court Division as referred to by the learned Advocate we find no reason to interfere with the same.
